Back: Controls who can do what in AWS. Users · groups · roles · policies. KEYWORDS: least privilege · trust policy · instance profile · SCP · permission boundary · explicit deny. TRADE-OFF: Broad permissions = fast setup but large blast radius. Least privilege = slower but limits damage.

Temporary identity for AWS services — no long-lived credentials. KEYWORDS: assume role · trust policy · instance profile · STS · no access keys. USE WHEN: EC2 needs S3, Lambda needs DynamoDB, cross-account access.

Manage multiple accounts. SCPs = hard limits on what any account in an OU can do. KEYWORDS: OU · management account · SCP · guardrail · consolidated billing. TRADE-OFF: One wrong SCP can break an account — test carefully.

Logically isolated private network. Resources unreachable by default. KEYWORDS: subnet · route table · Internet Gateway · NAT Gateway · CIDR · private/public · peering · Transit Gateway. TRADE-OFF: CIDR blocks are hard to change after creation — plan upfront.

Stateful firewall at the resource level (EC2, RDS, ALB). KEYWORDS: stateful · inbound/outbound · allow only · no explicit deny · port 22 · port 443. TRADE-OFF: No explicit deny — misconfigured rule silently opens access.

Stateless subnet-level firewall. Must allow BOTH inbound AND outbound explicitly. KEYWORDS: stateless · subnet-level · explicit allow AND deny · rule number. TRADE-OFF: Forgetting return traffic breaks connections.

Manages encryption keys. Never exposes raw key material. KEYWORDS: CMK · AWS managed key · customer managed key · key policy · envelope encryption · rotation · CloudTrail audit. TRADE-OFF: AWS Managed Keys are free. CMKs cost $1/month but give you control.

Stores and auto-rotates secrets. Apps fetch at runtime — no secrets in code. KEYWORDS: automatic rotation · Lambda rotation · versioning · cross-account. USE WHEN: DB passwords · API keys · any credential that should never be in source.

DDoS protection. Standard = free + automatic. Advanced = $3k/month + SRT access. KEYWORDS: DDoS · Layer 3/4 · SYN flood · volumetric · SRT · cost protection. EXAM: Standard always on. Advanced for high-profile targets and SLA guarantees.

Layer 7 HTTP firewall. Blocks SQL injection, XSS, bots, rate-limits. KEYWORDS: Web ACL · managed rules · OWASP Top 10 · rate limit · SQL injection · XSS · attach to CloudFront/ALB/API Gateway. TRADE-OFF: Managed rules fast but can false-positive.

Behavioral threat detection using ML on CloudTrail + VPC Flow Logs + DNS. KEYWORDS: behavioral · ML · findings · Tor exit node · crypto mining · 30-day free trial. TRADE-OFF: Detects anomalies but requires human review to respond.

Records every API call: who · what · when · from where · result. KEYWORDS: audit · 90-day default · S3 trail · log integrity validation · management events · data events. USE WHEN: Compliance, forensics, security baseline.

ML-based sensitive data discovery in S3 (PII, credentials, financial). KEYWORDS: PII · sensitive data · S3 classification · data privacy. MACIE vs GUARDDUTY: Macie finds sensitive DATA. GuardDuty finds suspicious BEHAVIOR.

Spread resources across Availability Zones. One AZ fails → others serve traffic. KEYWORDS: AZ failure · standby · automatic failover · RPO ≈ 0 · RTO < 2 min · same region. TRADE-OFF: Roughly doubles cost but protects against most common AWS failure.

Replication to a second AWS Region. Protects against full regional outages. KEYWORDS: RPO · RTO · pilot light · warm standby · active-active · Aurora Global · Route 53 failover. TRADE-OFF: Much higher cost/complexity than Multi-AZ. Validate business case first.

Automatically adds/removes EC2 based on load. Replaces unhealthy instances. KEYWORDS: launch template · target tracking · min/max/desired · health check · cooldown · warm pool. TRADE-OFF: Takes minutes to scale — pre-warm with Warm Pools for faster response.

Layer 7 load balancer. Routes HTTP/HTTPS by path/host/header. KEYWORDS: Layer 7 · target group · listener rule · path routing · sticky sessions · health check · WAF attachment. ALB vs NLB: ALB for HTTP/HTTPS. NLB for TCP/UDP/extreme performance.

Fully managed message queue. Decouples producers from consumers. KEYWORDS: queue · message · visibility timeout · DLQ · at-least-once · FIFO · Standard · polling · decoupling. Standard: high throughput + possible duplicates. FIFO: ordered + exactly-once + 3k msg/s.

Pub/sub. One publisher → many subscribers (SQS, Lambda, email, SMS, HTTP). KEYWORDS: topic · fan-out · push · SQS+SNS pattern. SNS vs SQS: SNS pushes to all subscribers. SQS stores for one consumer to pull.

Serverless functions. Runs code on events. Pay per invocation + per ms. KEYWORDS: serverless · cold start · 15-min limit · stateless · SQS/S3/API Gateway trigger · provisioned concurrency · reserved concurrency. TRADE-OFF: Zero idle cost but cold starts add latency.

Orchestrates multi-step workflows as state machines. Handles retries, tracks state. KEYWORDS: state machine · retry · catch · execution history · Standard (90-day) · Express (5-min) · idempotency. Standard: durable + auditable. Express: fast + cheap + no audit.

Runs Docker containers. Fargate (serverless) or EC2 (managed hosts). KEYWORDS: task definition · ECS service · Fargate · ECR · task IAM role · service auto scaling. ECS vs EKS: ECS for AWS-native simplicity. EKS if you need Kubernetes ecosystem.
Managed Kubernetes control plane. KEYWORDS: Kubernetes · control plane · worker nodes · pod · Fargate profile. USE WHEN: Migrating existing K8s workloads or team already knows Kubernetes.

Virtual machines in the cloud. Full control over OS and configuration. KEYWORDS: instance type · AMI · key pair · instance profile · On-Demand · Reserved · Spot · placement group · UserData. TRADE-OFF: Maximum control = maximum management responsibility.

Object storage. Any file in buckets. 11-nines durability. Unlimited scale. KEYWORDS: bucket · object · key · eleven-nines · versioning · lifecycle · storage class · presigned URL · event notification. NOT a filesystem — can't mount. Latency higher than EBS.

Persistent block storage for ONE EC2 instance. KEYWORDS: volume · snapshot · gp3 · io2 · AZ-bound · one instance · IOPS · throughput · encryption. TRADE-OFF: Tied to one AZ. Must snapshot for backup or cross-AZ migration.

Managed NFS filesystem. Mounts to MULTIPLE EC2 instances simultaneously. KEYWORDS: NFS · shared · multi-instance · elastic · Bursting/Provisioned throughput. TRADE-OFF: Higher cost than EBS. Use only when multiple instances need the same data.

Managed relational database (PostgreSQL/MySQL/etc). AWS handles patching, backups, failover. KEYWORDS: Multi-AZ · read replica · automated backups · PITR · RDS Proxy · no OS access. TRADE-OFF: No OS access. Write scaling requires Aurora or sharding.

AWS-built MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible DB. Shared storage (6 copies / 3 AZs). 5× faster than MySQL. KEYWORDS: shared storage · read replicas (15) · Aurora Global · Serverless v2 · Backtrack · ~30s failover. TRADE-OFF: Higher base cost than RDS. Worth it at scale.

Fully managed NoSQL. Single-digit ms latency at any scale. KEYWORDS: partition key · sort key · GSI · LSI · on-demand · provisioned · DynamoDB Streams · DAX · hot partition. TRADE-OFF: No joins. Access patterns must be designed upfront.

Managed in-memory cache (Redis or Memcached). Reduces database load. KEYWORDS: Redis · Memcached · cache hit/miss · TTL · eviction · sub-ms latency. TRADE-OFF: Eventually consistent. Cache invalidation is the hard part.

CDN. Caches content at 400+ edge locations globally. KEYWORDS: edge location · origin · cache behavior · TTL · invalidation · Lambda@Edge · WAF attachment. TRADE-OFF: Cached content can go stale until TTL expires — set TTL carefully.

AWS DNS. Registers domains. Routes globally with health checks. KEYWORDS: hosted zone · A/CNAME/alias record · health check · failover · latency/weighted/geo routing · TTL. USE WHEN: DNS failover, multi-region routing, domain registration.

Real-time streaming. Multiple consumers read the same stream. KEYWORDS: shard · producer · consumer · replay · retention · partition key · Enhanced Fan-Out. Kinesis vs SQS: Kinesis = replay + multiple consumers. SQS = one consumer, message deleted after read.

Serverless ETL. Discovers schemas (Crawler), stores metadata (Data Catalog), runs Spark jobs. KEYWORDS: ETL · crawler · Data Catalog · Spark · serverless · Parquet · partition. USE WHEN: Building data pipelines and transforming S3 data for analytics.

Serverless SQL on S3. Pay per TB scanned. KEYWORDS: serverless SQL · S3 · Parquet · partition · $5/TB · Glue Data Catalog · Workgroups. TRADE-OFF: Parquet + partitions can cut scan cost 99%. Without them, queries can be surprisingly expensive.
Pay per hour/second. No commitment. Most expensive. KEYWORDS: no commitment · per second · flexible. USE WHEN: Short-term, unpredictable workloads. Dev/test.

1 or 3 year commitment. Up to 72% discount. KEYWORDS: 1-year · 3-year · Standard RI · Convertible RI · Compute Savings Plan · break-even ~7 months. USE WHEN: Predictable 24/7 workloads. Production servers and databases.

Spare AWS capacity. Up to 90% discount. 2-minute interruption warning. KEYWORDS: 2-minute warning · checkpoint · Spot Fleet · not for databases · not for critical APIs. USE WHEN: Fault-tolerant, stateless, interruptible — batch jobs, CI/CD, data processing.

Standard (frequent) · Standard-IA (monthly) · Glacier Instant (rare, fast) · Glacier Flexible (rare, hours) · Deep Archive (never, 12h) · Intelligent-Tiering (unknown). RULE: Lower per-GB → retrieval fee. Intelligent-Tiering: no retrieval fee but per-object monitoring charge.

Lets private subnet resources reach internet outbound. Internet cannot connect inbound. KEYWORDS: outbound only · per-hour + per-GB · one per AZ for HA · VPC Gateway Endpoint avoids NAT for S3/DynamoDB. TRADE-OFF: Per-GB fee adds up fast at scale.

Private connection to AWS services — no internet, no NAT. Gateway (S3/DynamoDB — FREE). Interface (other services — $/hr). KEYWORDS: no internet · PrivateLink · Gateway free · Interface priced. ALWAYS use Gateway Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB.

AWS secures OF the cloud (hardware, data centers, global network). YOU secure IN the cloud (data, IAM, app config, OS patching on EC2). KEY NUANCE: More managed service = more AWS responsibility. RDS: AWS patches DB. EC2: you patch OS.

RTO = Recovery Time Objective: how long system can be DOWN. RPO = Recovery Point Objective: how much DATA you can lose. RPO=0 → synchronous replication (Multi-AZ). Aurora Global is ASYNC: RPO ~1s, not 0. RTO<2min → Multi-AZ. RTO<seconds → active-active multi-region.

CapEx = buy hardware upfront, depreciate over time (on-premises). OpEx = pay as you go monthly (cloud). EXAM SIGNAL: 'eliminate upfront costs' or 'shift from CapEx to OpEx' → cloud adoption answer.
